newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends lower on profit-taking, stocks.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends lower on profit-taking, stocks.

text.p: COMEX copper ended weaker as end of week booksquaring and a sharp hike in LME stocks Friday took their toll, traders said.
LME stocks rose 15,325 tonnes to 215,825 tonnes.
"The stock increase was a good deal higher than the traders' estimated and ultimately the market responded to that," Bette Raptopoulos of Prudential Securities said.
"The market is going to be choppy because of the warehouse stocks, but trending higher," Raptopoulos said.
Brokers said that producer selling was also noted, putting a lid on price gains after LME three months failed to break through $2,270 per tonne.
March COMEX ended 1.45 cents weaker at 107.15 cents per pound, traded 109.30 to 105.60 cents. Volume was estimated at 12,000 lots compared to Thursday's official 10,382 lots.
The LME cash premium over three months or backwardation also eased on Friday, down about $25 to $200/$210.
Brokers said the tightness on LME appeared to be rolling over into early March, some two weeks longer than originally anticipated by some traders.
